clue.text: End of crisis — allowed out of bed?

definitions.meaning: a lull or easing when pressure relaxes
permitted to get up, like a recovering patient

explanation.definitionFit: A lull or easing is a let-up; someone permitted to rise from bed has been let up.

clue.text: Have nowhere for home matches, and fall behind?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, to be deprived of one's sports ground
to slip back relative to others

explanation.definitionFit: A club deprived of its pitch is literally without a ground; the idiom means slipping back.

clue.text: Brew a drop? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a tear is a drop from the eye

explanation.surface: Is a drop of liquid enough to make a brew? Not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic British brew, made by steeping leaves.

clue.text: Set about looking up man's address, being scrupulous

definitions.note: read as a scrupulous being, a person

indicators.note: about means the word for set goes around the other piece

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sir is how a man is addressed

explanation.surface: Someone sets about examining a man's speech with great scrupulousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's address' reads like a street address, but it is the form of address used to a man. 'being scrupulous' works as a noun: a scrupulous being.
explanation.definitionFit: A purist insists on strict correctness, a scrupulous person.

clue.text: Go on crime spree, operating with maximum efficiency

indicators.note: a spree is a wild bout of activity, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook goes on a crime spree, working with ruthless efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spree' rearranges the nine letters of GO ON CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design arranges work so people operate with the least effort and greatest efficiency.

clue.text: Mere ship floundering without eastern navigational aid?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation
floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A mere ship floundering with no eastern bearing needs navigational help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' rearranges MERE SHIP, and 'without' wraps that around E. 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephemeris tables the positions of heavenly bodies, used by navigators to fix position.

clue.text: Old king detaining individual, a person about to depart

indicators.note: detaining means the king's letters hold the other word inside

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George
an individual is one

explanation.surface: An old king detains someone who is about to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or about to die, colloquially.

clue.text: Item of ID — paid for copy to be attached to new article.

indicators.note: to be attached to means these pieces follow on after the new article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to meet a cost is to pay it, so paid for is met
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: An ID tag is paid for, and a copy is attached to a new item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid for' is the past tense of meeting a bill; the clue's order is reversed by the attaching phrase, so the new article leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tape is a label sewn into clothing to identify its owner.

clue.text: Metronome I'm activating -— it hints at the passage of time

definitions.text: it hints at the passage of time

indicators.note: activating sets the letters in motion, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A musician starts a metronome ticking, a reminder of time passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activating' rearranges the letters of METRONOME I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento mori, Latin for remember you must die, is an object that reminds us of mortality.

clue.text: Conservative remains ready

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Conservative remains ever prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like an adjective, but the ready is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The ready, or readies, is British slang for available money.

clue.text: Cruise, and mostly hang about to see marine creature

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around into a fresh order
most of the word hang is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Take a cruise and mostly lounge about, and you may spot sea life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims hang to HAN; 'about' then rearranges CRUISE plus HAN. 'Cruise' looks like a synonym to find, but it is fodder as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny echinoderm living on the seabed, a marine creature.

clue.text: Everything about head of Government reflected disease

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the whole construction is read backwards
about means the word for everything goes around the other piece

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount, everything
the PM, Prime Minister, heads the British government

explanation.surface: A head of government reflects on a disease spreading everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of Government' looks like a first-letter pick, but it is the Prime Minister's abbreviation; 'reflected' turns the whole container round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a contagious viral illness causing swollen glands, a disease.

clue.text: Woman into wares displayed by a chap, a helpful type

parts.note: wares are goods for sale

indicators.note: into means the woman's name goes inside the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a man
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman inspects goods on display from a man, who proves very obliging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' is only a link joining the wares to the rest; the woman's name splits the chap after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a Good Samaritan is anyone who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Married, it seems, and taking it as it comes?

definitions.meaning: no longer left unwed, as when a spinster was said to be on the shelf
bought as stocked, standard rather than custom-made

explanation.definitionFit: Goods taken straight from stock are ready-made; a woman no longer unwed is likewise taken.

clue.text: Computer item not of major interest

definitions.meaning: a device such as a printer attached to a computer

explanation.definitionFit: A printer or mouse is a computer add-on; anything marginal is minor, on the edges.

clue.text: Composer's Ring runs very loud

definitions.note: read as 'Composer is', the 's standing for is

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A composer's Ring cycle is played at deafening volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Ring calls up Wagner's opera cycle, but the composer is a different German: Carl Orff.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana.

clue.text: Assume schoolwork's set to hold us back

indicators.note: to hold means the schoolwork word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: prep is homework at a British boarding school; the 's is has

indicators.note: back means the word us is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to set a question is to pose it

explanation.surface: Assume homework has been set to keep us behind after school.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep is British boarding-school homework; 'set' is pose as in setting a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To presuppose something is to take it for granted beforehand, to assume it.

clue.text: Sort I have found under surface of sea and river?

definitions.text: Sort I have found under surface of sea and river?

indicators.note: found under means the following pieces sit below the letter from the sea, in this down answer
the surface of a word is its top, which in a down answer is its first letter

parts.note: a sort is a kind
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A kind of person found below the surface of seas and rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: such a swimmer is found below the surface of sea and river.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin diver swims underwater without a diving suit, often with just a mask.

clue.text: Total formality when bringing in a new partnership

parts.note: total means all

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for formality takes the other letters inside

parts.note: ice is cold formality or reserve, as in breaking the ice

explanation.surface: Total formality is observed when a new partnership is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' puts A and N inside ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or partnership between parties.

clue.text: One expects nothing to come of an idea like this

definitions.text: One expects nothing to come of an idea like this

parts.words: One expects nothing to come of an idea like this
parts.note: a cryptic description of a philosophy that rejects all values and expects nothing; the clue also plays on nothing coming of it

explanation.definitionFit: Nihilism holds that nothing has meaning or value, so such a view expects nothing.

clue.text: Conductor with no time for individual performances

indicators.note: with no means the time letter is removed from the conductor's name

parts.note: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor too busy to rehearse leaves players to perform on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Soli is the plural of solo, pieces or passages performed by one musician.

clue.text: New French name upset the German brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the German word goes inside the reversed name
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: nom is French for name
der is the German for the

explanation.surface: A new French name upset the German who was introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down clue turns the French word upside down, so it reads upwards; the German article then sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means new or up to date.

clue.text: Good clean activity associated with old buffers?

definitions.text: Good clean activity associated with old buffers?

parts.words: Good clean activity associated with old buffers?
parts.note: buffers are polishing pads, but old buffers are also fusty old men such as retired soldiers, fond of military-style shining of boots

explanation.definitionFit: Spit and polish is thorough cleaning and smartness, especially of military kit.

clue.text: Recognise it supports a former European currency

indicators.note: in a down clue supports means sitting below, so this piece comes last

parts.note: DM, the Deutschmark, was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Admit that it underpins a currency of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' comes first in the clue but 'supports' puts it at the bottom, after A and DM.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit or acknowledge something is to recognise it.

clue.text: Leader of army out of step, causing commotion

indicators.note: out of means that letter is taken from the step word

parts.note: a stair is a step

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An army leader marching out of step causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of step' looks like a phrase, but 'out of' removes A from STAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a disturbance or fuss, a commotion.

clue.text: Programme link that is in the can

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the word for can

parts.note: a can is a tin
IE (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: The programme link-up, that is, is in the can, already recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the can' suggests finished filming; here can is just TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a product or programme linked to another, such as a book of a series.

clue.text: One may be kept in the dark before getting the picture

definitions.text: One may be kept in the dark before getting the picture

parts.words: One may be kept in the dark before getting the picture
parts.note: sounds like someone left uninformed until they understand, but describes a person sitting in a darkened cinema before the film starts

explanation.definitionFit: A cinema patron sits in darkness waiting for the film, or picture, to begin.

clue.text: Item of insignia in gold and black

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A piece of regalia is fashioned in gold and black.
explanation.definitionFit: The orb is a jewelled sphere among the royal regalia carried by a monarch.

clue.text: One thinking of a telescope

definitions.meaning: a person who reflects or ponders
a type of telescope that uses a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ponders reflects; a mirror-based telescope is called by the same name.

clue.text: Prize title? No. — a boxing award's cut

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number, here taken as the letters N and O

indicators.note: cut means the final letter of the award is chopped off

parts.note: a boxing champion is awarded a belt; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A prize title is refused: a boxer's award has been withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel name heads a set of international prizes founded by Alfred Nobel.
